scope: Bounded factual review of the final visible article and held suggestions against primary GitHub records and pinned repository sources; no article revision or acceptance, finding disposition, action admission or settlement, readiness or merge, workflow dispatch, runtime or schedule change.

findings.title: BookcaseDiscovery ran 92 files and 1,959 tests, not 91 and 195
findings.location: Line 49 says the full run covered all 91 files and surfaced 195 passing tests, with 89 files passing and 3 skipped.
findings.explanation: BookcaseDiscovery #106 records 92 files: 89 passed and 3 skipped, with 1,959 tests passed and 18 skipped. The article's own file split totals 92.
findings.correction: Report 92 collected files, 89 passed and 3 skipped, with 1,959 passing tests and 18 skipped tests, attributed to #106.

findings.title: A misnamed test file is excluded, not silently included
findings.location: Line 87 says a misnamed file silently joins the suite, then says a file outside the naming convention is silently excluded.
findings.explanation: Core #727's guard covers tracked files matching the named test patterns. A file outside those patterns is not discovered; #728 separately records deliberate command and filter bypasses.
findings.correction: Say a correctly named file joins automatically while a misnamed file can be silently excluded; remove the contradictory sentence.

findings.title: Known bypasses remain; the sweep did not eliminate every false-green path
findings.location: The title and opening say false greens were eliminated across five repos, and line 57 says all five audited every exit path.
findings.explanation: Core #728 and BookcaseDiscovery #107 list concrete, still-open bypasses in the new guards, including deliberate named-file or filter edits, unchecked trigger types and needs, and shell control-flow changes.
findings.correction: Say the interval closed the identified accidental false-green paths and added structural guards, while deliberate bypasses remain tracked in #728 and #107.

findings.title: cca-prep #40 was open, not landed
findings.location: Line 113 says the LCAE pack landed this interval; line 127 calls it in review.
findings.explanation: cca-prep #40 remained open and unmerged at the reviewed source revision.
findings.correction: Say the LCAE pack opened for review and filed gaps #29–#39; do not call it landed until the PR merges.

findings.title: One grilling ticket was closed, and the open prototype is omitted
findings.location: The retained context at line 154 says nine grilling tickets #736–#743 and #746 are all open.
findings.explanation: Core #737 was closed with an owner ruling before generation. #744 is an open prototype. #745 records the earlier set as eight grilling tickets and one prototype; #746 was added later as another grilling ticket.
findings.correction: Report eight open grilling tickets, one closed grilling ticket (#737), and one open prototype (#744).

findings.title: PRs #606 and #607 already identify their reviewer, findings and next step
findings.location: Lines 129–136 call #606/#607 audits with no reviewer or close event; the held candidate at line 146 proposes viewing them to discover their disposition.
findings.explanation: Both PR bodies name the Codex independent reviewer, exact source/blob, finding counts, validation and scope. Their exact-source handoff comments record that they intentionally remain Draft with findings open and await supervised disposition.
findings.correction: Say both reviews are complete as bounded Draft review-data proposals and await supervised finding disposition; do not propose a duplicate lookup as new work.

findings.title: The named journal range contains seven open service/journal slices, not six
findings.location: Line 132 calls #575–#584 six journal refactor slices.
findings.explanation: The open service/journal Drafts are #575, #576 and #580–#584: seven. #577 is a closed integration PR, #578 is the article PR and #579 is a review PR.
findings.correction: Report seven open service/journal Drafts in the range and distinguish #577–#579 as non-slice PRs.

findings.title: Only the legacy skill stream is frozen; the collector uses the live dispositions ledger
findings.location: The retained context at line 155 says the stream is frozen since 2026-05-12 and treats 0% quality coverage as a lower bound for that reason.
findings.explanation: The pinned collector makes skill-dispositions.jsonl the live primary source and uses the frozen skill-telemetry.jsonl only as a fallback; live disposition invocations are included in quality coverage.
findings.correction: Distinguish the live dispositions ledger from the frozen legacy fallback and report the collector's recorded source and freshness.

findings.title: The held Bookcase command can hide a failing test run and repeats completed validation
findings.location: The fourth held candidate at line 146 pipes pnpm test to head -40 and says it should list all 91 files and preserve failure.
findings.explanation: BookcaseDiscovery #106 already records the guard and full-suite run with 92 files. Bash returns the last pipeline command's status unless pipefail is enabled, so head can report success after pnpm test fails; with pipefail, truncation can instead surface upstream SIGPIPE.
findings.correction: Use #106 as the existing receipt. If a fresh supervised run is needed, run pnpm check:ci-tests && pnpm test without the truncating pipeline, or capture output separately while preserving the test command's status.

findings.title: No fleet-wide pre-fix CI baseline was established by the checked evidence
findings.location: Line 61 says the fleet has no CI coverage baseline predating today's fixes that it can defend.
findings.explanation: Core #727 and BookcaseDiscovery #106 establish gaps in those two repos, not the nonexistence of any defensible baseline across the whole fleet. The bounded review found no exhaustive fleet inventory proving that negative.
findings.correction: Limit the claim to the two documented repos or cite an exhaustive fleet baseline audit; until then label the fleet-wide absence unverified.

findings.title: The trust-build roadmap does not visibly record the asserted CI prerequisite
findings.location: Lines 59 and 105 say PH8–PH13 depends on every automation step failing closed and that this prerequisite is recorded in the Core trust-build plan.
findings.explanation: The pinned PH8–PH13 roadmap records authority service, enforcement, outside review, evidence, stops and tests goals, but the checked plan does not state this specific CI-integrity prerequisite. #727 and #728 do not establish a PH8 entrance dependency.
findings.correction: Cite the exact plan line that records this prerequisite or describe the connection as an interpretation rather than a recorded gate.
